text:
sasha: Quick heads-up 30 onboarding note: windfall9b HF->internal conversion + our int4 quant shows notable perf delta on summarization and next-token perplexity. Suspect architecture layout mismatch.
ryan: Numbers? rough delta?
sasha: Small table from the smoke evals:
```
model                 | rouge1 | ppl (next-token) | latency/token
windfall9b-fp16       | 0.45   | 9.3              | 11.8ms
windfall9b-int4       | 0.36   | 12.7             | 5.8ms
windfall9b-int4-rotmask| 0.40  | 10.8             | 6.0ms
```
sasha: So int4 baseline drops ~20% R1 and jumps ppl; enabling a per-head rotary mask recovered ~half the loss.
ekta: Interesting. Did the conversion preserve head ordering? We recently hit cases where converters squash heterogeneous head splits into "regular groups" and that breaks rotary indexing.
sasha: I dumped the model proto vs converted header:
```
# on-disk header: 
num_heads: 48
head_splits: [12,12,12,12]   # converter-normalized
# upstream HF metadata:
num_heads: 48
per_head_dims: [32,32,16,48]  # heterogeneous head_dim groups (weird)
head_map: [0..47]  # explicit mapping present
```
sasha: The converter normalized to 4 groups (all equal), losing per_head_dims. Our runtime built cos/sin tables assuming contiguous same-dim head blocks.
jules: That would definitely misapply rotary angles: the sin/cos table index = head_index * head_dim, so if head_dim mapping is wrong the cosine phase aligns to wrong subvector.
ekta: Does the kv-cache path also assume uniform head_dim? If cache strides are wrong we could be reading/writing offsets incorrectly and amplify quant noise.
sasha: Cache stride is computed from projected head_dim after conversion; since conversion forced uniform 32 it wrote kv entries with that stride. When actual runtime projections produce mixed-sized chunks, the mapping is off.
ryan: Concrete mitigation: 1) quick fix: preserve explicit head_map and per_head_dims in converter and plumb it through runtime so sin/cos table computed per-head by mapping. 2) short-term safety: during int4 quant, disable per-head rotary (apply absolute pos proj) or apply a fallback uniformization layer that reorders/concats heads to match converted layout.
jules: Another experiment: re-run quant but with random 1-token warmup using fp16 cache values to see if warmup reduces drift. That may isolate whether cold-cache quantization amplification is to blame.
ekta: Also run a logit-diff histogram on top-k tokens across 200 eval prompts (we have a small bench that computes KL per token). Helps decide if model shifts probability mass systematically (e.g., prefers shorter completions).
sasha: OK running the following jobs now:
 - 1755565000-01: reconvert-preserve-headmap + int4 quant (queue)
 - 1755565000-02: int4 quant + rotary-disabled fallback (bench quick)
 - 1755565000-03: logit-diff/topk + KL per-step (200 prompts)
bench-bot: Queued jobs: 1755565000-01, 1755565000-02, 1755565000-03. Expected ~45-90m depending on GPU queue.
ryan: If reconversion fixes it, add a CR to model-converter to retain per_head_dims and run unit tests: roundtrip head_map -> sincos index verification. Add a small synthetic: generate sincos for random head_map and ensure indexing matches projection offsets.
jules: Also flag Dedicated customers with pinned older quant profile? Might need a short-lived compatibility note: models with heterogenous head dims require converter >= v0.12 to avoid int4 regressions.
ekta: Good point. For now we can gate the auto-quant pipeline to warn and skip int4 for models whose converter produced head_map normalization mismatch.
sasha: Will post run outputs when done. If rotary-disabled keeps most quality we can ship a temporary runtime gate while we patch converter.
ryan: Ping when you have the logit diffs, and include a sample prompt that diverged badly so we can inspect attention maps.
sasha: Will do. Thanks all :mechanical_arm:
